info.title: Ductura API
info.description:
Shared errors: any route may answer these besides the errors listed under it.
- 500 internal: problem body {error, code, messageKey: "errors.internal", status, requestId}.
- 429 too_many_requests: problem body {error, code, messageKey: "errors.tooManyRequests", status, requestId}; header retry-after in whole seconds.
- 401 session_idle_expired: problem body {error, code, messageKey: "errors.sessionIdleExpired", status, requestId}.

post.summary: OIDC back-channel logout: the provider posts a signed logout token, no cookie.

get.summary: Return from the identity provider; checks state and PKCE, opens the session.
Starts AAI@EduHr login (PKCE); returnTo is narrowed to a safe local path.

post.summary: Closes every session of the caller; on failure keeps the cookie.
Closes the current session. Same Origin only; an empty body.
Confirms the caller's security key against an assertion challenge. 403 for a key that is not the caller's or is revoked; 409 when the signature counter fell or stayed the same (0 to 0 is accepted).

400.description: content_length_invalid, content_length_mismatch, body_stream_error, invalid_json, challenge_invalid, ceremony_invalid

post.summary: A one-time challenge of 32 random bytes for one ceremony of this session, registration or assertion. It expires after timeoutMs and is spent by the first attempt, successful or not.

200.description: challenge issued; the purpose picks the shape

post.summary: Registers the caller's security key (ES256, COSE -7; attestation none) against a registration challenge; the key is the COSE key in authenticatorData. 403 when the account already has a key, 409 when the key is registered.

400.description: content_length_invalid, content_length_mismatch, body_stream_error, invalid_json, challenge_invalid, ceremony_invalid

post.summary: Records the client's environment (D-300): app, version, system, browser, device and a screen width class, each from a closed list. Works without a login, under the rate limit; the body is the JCS form of the value, and any other field, value or form is 400 invalid_input. Never used to decide access.

Comments on a work (B-10). The action picks the body: create {anchor, body, documentId} and reply {body, threadId} answer 200 {id}; resolve and reopen {threadId} and delete {commentId} answer 204; list {documentId} answers 200 {comments}. Exactly those keys, at most 16 KiB; an unknown action is 404. The database decides who may read or write (403); a thread that changed in the meantime is 409.

200.description: the new comment's id (create, reply) or the comments (list)

post.summary: Revision requests on a work (DAN-314). The action picks the body, as its exact JCS bytes, at most 16 KiB: create {anchor, documentId, instruction, requestedRevision} answers 200 {request_id, row_seq, version, state}; respond, accept, reopen, rereview and withdraw (with requestId and expectedSeq) answer 200 {outcome: "applied", row_seq, version, state}, or 409 {outcome: "conflict", row_seq, version, state} when expectedSeq is stale; list {documentId} answers 200 {requests}. A malformed id reads as a foreign one (403); a transition the state does not allow is 409 not_allowed; an unknown action is 404.

409.description: expectedSeq is stale: the current counter, version and state; not_allowed

get.summary: The desktop packages a client may offer: one row per system and architecture at most, by system then architecture. url is a path on this address or an https address; sha256 is the SHA-256 of the package bytes in lowercase hex, which the client checks before it opens the package. An empty list: no package yet. A manifest the server cannot read makes the answer 503, never a partial list.

200.description: manifest (an empty list when there is no package yet)

post.summary: One evidence segment and the document after it. Same Origin, `ductus-protocol: 1` (signed now, 200) or `2` (signed by the worker: 202 pending_signature, then the same request again).

202.description: stored, receipt pending_signature (protocol 2 only); not an acknowledgement

post.summary: The caller's own work for one assignment and its current revision; `start: true` makes it. Same Origin, `ductus-protocol: 1`; anyone but the student gets 404.

One page of the replay of a work: the verified stored bytes of its segments in chain order, as the JCS text of the page. The body is exactly {documentId, from: 0} for the first page and {documentId, from, head} for every later one, with the head the first page reported; any other shape is 422. Same Origin, `ductus-protocol: 1`. A work the caller may not read, an id that cannot exist or a page past the end is 404. A record that no longer ends at `head` is 409 record_changed (read again from the first page); a record that does not verify is 503, never a partial page.

200.description: one page, its JCS text unchanged

post.summary: The student acknowledges the notice of an assignment version they were shown. The body is exactly {versionNo, fingerprint}: the version and the SHA-256 the browser computed of the notice text, at most 1 KiB, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only), with no escape and no repeated key. A malformed assignment id is 400 invalid_assignment_id, judged before the session. A version that is no longer current is 409 conflict; a stored notice other than the one shown is 409 notice_changed, and nothing is recorded.

An administrator of the institution creates a course: exactly {name, academicYear, aiPolicy, holderId, groups}, at most 8 KiB, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only). holderId is a confirmed teacher of the same institution, who becomes the course's holder and a teacher of it; groups are the names of its seminar groups (0 to 20, distinct, each 1 to 80 UTF-16 units with no space at either end). The name is 1 to 160 UTF-16 units with no space at either end; the academic year is two consecutive years such as 2026/2027. A teacher who is not an administrator is 403. The same course (institution, academic year, name) sent again with the same content answers its id; with other content it is 409 conflict.

A teacher of the assignment publishes its next version against the version they saw: {expectedVersion} and the whole content, both word bounds named (null drops one), at most 90 000 bytes. A tightening of the rules, an AI purpose under a prohibited policy, wordMin above wordMax or an impossible date is 422; a stale version is 409 version_conflict, and of two requests with the same version one writes.

get.summary: The current version of an assignment, for a teacher of its course: its number and whole content as institution.assignment-versions.post takes it, instants as Date.toISOString writes them. groupIds, externalToolsAllowed and aiSummaryOnly are those of the creation, absent until the server stores them. Sec-Fetch-Site, when sent, other than same-origin is 403; a malformed id is 422; another course's assignment, an unknown one and any caller who is not a teacher of its course are the same 404 (C-23). A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503.

post.summary: A teacher of the course creates and publishes an assignment (version 1) with its rules on AI tools (aiPolicy and aiPurposes, A-14): {requestKey} and the whole content, at most 90 000 bytes, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only). requestKey is a UUID the client makes once per form, in the body so the generated client sends it. The same key with the same content answers the same id; with other content it is 409 conflict. A malformed course id or key, a tightening the course forbids, an AI purpose under a prohibited policy, wordMin above wordMax or an impossible date is 422. Publishing sends nothing to anyone (C-17): students see it in student.assignments.get. Optional: groupIds, the course's seminar groups it is for (absent or empty: the whole course); externalToolsAllowed (outside tools, absent false); aiSummaryOnly (the AI assistant only summarises, absent false). A group of another course or one named twice, and aiSummaryOnly under a prohibited policy or with any aiPurposes, are 422.

A teacher of the course team or an administrator of the institution assigns a confirmed teacher of the institution to a seminar group: exactly {teacherId}, at most 1 KiB. The teacher joins the course team through the group. assigned is false when they already teach the group. A teacher who is not confirmed is 422.

get.summary: The seminar groups of a course, for a teacher of its team or an administrator of its institution: by name (hr collation), then id, each with its open teachers (by family and given name, hr collation, then id) and the number of its open students; no student is named. A malformed course id is 422. Another institution's course and an unknown one are the same 403 (C-23).

post.summary: The holder, a collaborator of the course team (C-7) or an administrator of the institution adds a seminar group: exactly {name}, 1 to 80 UTF-16 units with no space at either end, at most 1 KiB. A group of the same name answers its id; nothing is made twice. A student is 403.

A teacher creates a course in their institution: exactly {name, academicYear, aiPolicy}, at most 2 KiB, sent as application/json (only the media type before any parameter is judged). The name is 1 to 160 UTF-16 units with no space at either end; the academic year is two consecutive years such as 2026/2027. The same course sent again answers its id, never a second course.
A teacher of the course revokes its enrolment code. The body is exactly {}; revoked is false when there was no code to revoke.

get.summary: Whether the course has an enrolment code, for a teacher of the course: current is the code last issued and not revoked, with its validUntil (Date.toISOString), or null when none was issued or it was revoked. A current code past validUntil is still current: the client shows it as expired. The code itself is never sent (A-8). Sec-Fetch-Site, when sent, other than same-origin is 403; a malformed id is 422; another institution's course, an unknown one and any caller who is not a teacher of the course are the same 404 (C-23).

post.summary: A teacher of the course issues its enrolment code, valid until {validUntil}, replacing any earlier one; at most 1 KiB. The instant keeps its offset and fraction as sent; an impossible date or one the database refuses is 422.

Enrols the caller in the course of a code. The body is exactly {code}, at most 64 UTF-16 units and 1 KiB, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only). A wrong or expired code is 422 refused; too many guesses are 429 too_many_attempts, and each guess counts even when refused.

An administrator of the institution confirms one candidate as a teacher. The body is exactly {}. A caller who is not an administrator is 403; for an administrator every candidate that cannot be confirmed (themself, another institution's, a missing one, one whose last login gave no right) is the same 404.

An administrator of the institution ends one person's confirmed teacher role. The body is exactly {}; revoked is false when that person holds no active confirmed teacher role in the caller's institution, so another institution's person looks the same as a missing one.
A teacher of the course ends one student's membership. The body is exactly {}; removed is false when that user holds no open student membership there.
A teacher of the course lets one removed student enrol again; the student still needs a valid code. The body is exactly {}; allowed is false when nothing was blocking that student there.
One work's exception from the language of its assignment, keyed by the student; {language: null} removes it. At most 128 bytes. Answers the language the work has afterwards.

200.description: the language the work has now

post.summary: A teacher of the assignment sets the language its works are written in, against the version they saw: {expectedVersion, language}, at most 128 bytes, sent as application/json (only the media type before any parameter is judged). A malformed assignment id is 422; a stale version or a work already asked to be submitted is 409 conflict. Answers the new version.

The same exception keyed by the work's document id, so the student's id never reaches the browser; a document that is not a work of this teacher's assignment is refused like another teacher's (403). A malformed document id is 422, judged after the content type and the body.

200.description: the language the work has now

get.summary: The last published state of a work, the same bytes and ETag for the owner and the teacher. The request carries `ductus-protocol: 1` (and Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin when the browser sends it), else 403; a teacher's read writes the access log. `If-None-Match: "<etag>"` with the ETag last read answers 304. After the submission the bytes are the submitted revision, marked `ductus-live-state: submitted`. 204 when nothing is published yet.

304.description: the state of the ETag sent

put.summary: Publishes the last state of a work (the student owner only). The body is the exact JCS bytes of a valid document snapshot, at most 2 MiB. The request carries exactly one precondition: `If-None-Match: *` for the first write or `If-Match: "<token>"` with the last token, else 428. 200 {outcome, token} when accepted or unchanged; 409 {outcome: "conflict", token} with the current token (null when nothing is published yet) when the token is stale. The session is checked before the first body byte.

200.description: accepted, or the same state again

409.description: the token is stale: the current one, null when nothing is published

get.summary: Liveness: the process answers. Reads no database, session or environment.

200.description: alive. Since 1.3.0 also the state of the main database (`state`, checked with a time limit) and the versions; never an address, a name or an error.

state.description: degraded: the main database is not ok or did not answer in time

minClientVersion.description: oldest client version this server serves

get.summary: Readiness per capability, closed words only.
Public status in three parts, closed words, nothing about a person.
The caller's saved interface language, or null.

post.summary: Saves the caller's interface language. Canonical JSON, nothing but the locale.

get.summary: The caller's institution, roles in force and display name.

post.summary: The same accepted record for the owner and course teacher, with active editing minutes (sum of session spans excluding record gaps) and the coarse times of recorded imports and assistant transfers.

The process summary of one work, built from the accepted evidence only, as its JCS bytes. The body is exactly {documentId}, at most 1 KiB; any other key is 422. A work the caller may not read, or that does not exist, is 404; a record that does not verify is 503, never a partial summary.

Checks whether a signed submission receipt binds exactly the given text (C-6). The body is the two values of the receipt's QR fragment: the submission id and the SHA-256 of the submitted text, lowercase. Works without a login, never reads or sets a session cookie and is not a way to sign in (D-09); it has its own rate limit per address. match is true only when the institution's receipt for that submission names that hash and its Ed25519 signature verifies with a key valid then and not revoked; the answer then carries only the submission and signing instants and the key id, never a name, course, assignment or text. Every other case, an unknown submission included, is the same match false.

get.summary: The settings catalogue: every key, the levels that may hold it, its kind, default and hard limits.

The rows of one level in the caller's scope (course names the course for the course level and is absent for every other), and for every catalogue key of that level the value that holds without it (source: a higher level or default) and the narrowest higher bound. A level or course that is not the caller's gives 404, the same as a course that does not exist (C-23: another's is nonexistent).

200.description: the level's rows and what it inherits

put.summary: Sets the caller's value and bound of one key at one level (the bound as locked, min and max); no value and no bound remove the row and the level above holds again. course is a course id for the course level and null for every other. A level or course that is not the caller's gives 404, the same as a course that does not exist. A key outside the catalogue, a level the catalogue does not allow for it, a value of the wrong kind or out of its limits and a bound of a wrong shape give 422; crossing a higher bound gives 409. A refusal of the catalogue (422) comes before the level check (404), as in settings.set_value. 409 needs a key a lower level holds under a higher bound; the first catalogue has none, so its vector shows the shape only. Every change is kept with its author, time, old and new value.

200.description: saved (changed is false when the row already held it)

post.summary: Find bibliographic metadata for one DOI or ISBN in a catalogue, for synthetic students in local development.

200.description: Metadata for the source, or null when the catalogue has no record.

get.summary: Who opened the caller's own work and when (PRODUCT §5 rule 17): one entry per stored opening of five minutes, newest first; the client groups them into Europe/Zagreb days. No total of visits and no duration (D-274 MQ10). The query names the oldest entry shown, beforeAt and beforeId from next; a page from it holds only windows strictly older. Only both together, on the five-minute grid, a lowercase UUID, not in the future and not before year one are a cursor; anything else, and any other parameter, reads the first page with continued false, never an error, so every opening stays reachable. Another's work, an unknown and a malformed id read the same 404 (C-23). A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503.

200.description: a page of openings, possibly none

get.summary: The word range of the current assignment version. A null bound leaves that end open; when both bounds are present min is at most max. A null range means neither bound is set. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

The state of the caller's own work for every assignment student.assignments.get would list at the same instant: one row per assignment, by assignmentId (lowercase). submitted: the caller has a recorded submission for the assignment, of any of its versions; in_progress: the caller has a work for it (one per student and assignment) and no recorded submission; not_started: no work. The two reads are separate, so a client joins them by lowercase id and shows no state for an assignment without a row on both sides. The identity comes from the session only. A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503, never a partial list.

200.description: ready (an empty list when the student has no course)

get.summary: The courses of the caller's open student memberships and the current version of every assignment in each. Courses by name (hr collation), then id; assignments by due time, then id. The identity comes from the session only.

200.description: ready (an empty list when the student has no course)

get.summary: The student's own AI assistant conversation, messages by seq, each with the state of its request: a paragraph stays when its request ended without a response. Nobody else reads it, the teacher included. A foreign, unknown or malformed conversation id returns 404.

post.summary: A student of the assignment asks the AI assistant about one paragraph for one purpose. The Idempotency-Key header holds a UUID per account: the same key with the same request answers what is already there and never calls the provider again; with another request it answers idempotency_conflict. The provider and the model come from the server's versioned configuration and are never taken from the request; after a provider failure no other provider is tried. 200 always carries outcome from the closed set: completed with the response, or idempotency_conflict, forbidden (a foreign and an unknown assignment or conversation alike), ai_disabled, purpose_not_allowed, budget_exceeded, in_progress, request_outcome_unknown or provider_failed. A body outside the contract is 422 invalid_input (outcome invalid_request of the contract); a missing, repeated or malformed key is 428 precondition_required (outcome invalid_idempotency_key). Neither leaves a row, so the key stays free.

Enrols the caller in the course of a code. The body is exactly {code}, at most 64 UTF-16 units and 1 KiB, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only). The server normalizes the code (white space and hyphens removed, upper case); what is left must be 8 to 32 letters and digits, else it is invalid_code. outcome: enrolled; already_enrolled, the caller is a student of that course already and nothing changed; enrolled_no_assignment, enrolled in a course without an assignment yet. A code no course of the caller's institution has is 422 invalid_code; a code whose validity has ended is 422 expired_code. Too many guesses are 429 too_many_attempts, and each invalid or expired guess counts. The identity comes from the session only.

200.description: enrolled, already enrolled, or enrolled in a course without an assignment

post.summary: Records that the caller read the notice of the given version of an assignment of their open student membership (PO-7). The body is exactly {versionNo}, at most 128 bytes, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only). Idempotent: a repeated call answers the first readAt. A malformed assignment id is 400 invalid_assignment_id, judged before the session; another's assignment and an unknown one are the same 404 (C-23); a version that is no longer current is 409 conflict and nothing is recorded.

get.summary: The notice of the current version of an assignment of the caller's open student membership (E-6): the content of that version as the notice shows it, the notice template version, and when the caller first read it (PO-7, student.notice-read.post) and acknowledged it (institution.acknowledgment.post), each null until then. The fields are exactly those of the notice fingerprint (DAN-306), instants as Date.toISOString writes them; the browser computes the fingerprint from them and sends it with versionNo to institution.acknowledgment.post. aiPurposes is empty when aiPolicy is prohibited. The identity comes from the session only. Sec-Fetch-Site, when sent, other than same-origin is 403. Another's assignment, an unknown one and a malformed id are the same 404 (C-23). A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503.
Download the caller's signed submission receipt as a PDF. No signed receipt, an inaccessible assignment or a malformed id returns 404.

200.description: PDF bytes encoded in standard Base64, with a download filename

get.summary: The JPEG bytes of one proof of a source of the caller's own work. The proof is named by its work, source and id together; another student's work, another source or an unknown or malformed id return 404.

200.description: the JPEG bytes of the excerpt

get.summary: The proofs (attached excerpts) of one source of the caller's own work, oldest first, then by id. Another student's work, a source that is not in the work, an unknown or a malformed id return 404.

post.summary: Attaches an excerpt to a source of the caller's own work: a multipart form with the JPEG image (at most 1 MiB), the page and an optional note. Only an excerpt is kept: a whole PDF or any other file that is not a JPEG returns 422, as does a work at its bound (200 proofs or 100 MiB). Another student's work or a source that is not in the work returns 404.

get.summary: The caller's notes for an accessible assignment, oldest first, then by id.

post.summary: Adds a note for the caller's assignment. The text has 1 to 600 Unicode code points and contains a non-whitespace character. Notes are append-only and stay separate from the submission and signed receipt.

get.summary: The caller's submission for this assignment. An accessible assignment with no submission returns none. ceka means the submission was recorded but no signed receipt is attached yet. potvrdeno carries the same signed receipt as submission.submit.post. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

The text checks the caller's institution turns on (enabledCheckIds, in the order of the prototype) and its Lekta profile (lektaProfileId, null when the institution has set none). The answer holds no content of any work. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

delete.summary: Removes a source the caller added. A source that is not there, a teacher's source (with a requirement) and an inaccessible work all answer 404.

put.summary: Adds the caller's source or changes one the caller added; the source id is chosen by the client and must equal record.id. A work holds at most 500 sources. A source with a requirement is a teacher's: it is not changed here and answers 404, as does an inaccessible work.

get.summary: The sources of the caller's work on an accessible assignment, oldest first, then by id: the ones the caller added and the ones a teacher recommended or required (requirement). An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

post.summary: The student submits the revision they saw: exactly {documentId, revision}, at most 1 KiB; no time, text of the work or hash comes from the client. Same Origin, `ductus-protocol: 1`. The database clock at the click is the time; the revision is reconstructed and, only when it matches, the submission is recorded and its signed receipt returned. The first click binds: another revision later is 409 already_requested. Another student's or a missing work is 404. 503 carries the stage and `retry-after: 5`.

Sends a problem report: the user's description and a closed technical context. The body is the JCS form of the value, at most 8 KiB; the description is 1 to 1000 code points, no lone surrogate, with a visible character and no control or bidi character other than newline and tab (checked by the server, answered 422). The route is a page template; the server checks it against its closed list of 27 templates and answers 422 otherwise. At most five reports per account in an hour.

201.description: recorded; the reference the user quotes

get.summary: Whether the caller may see the teacher pages: a confirmed and unrevoked institution role (institution.actor_has_role('teacher')), never the login claims. The session and the role come from one snapshot, so denied is always an open session without the role and allowed always comes with a signed-in principal. scope is principalScope, for the shell of the teacher pages only; it is not the general source of the principal. No session is 401, a database that cannot be asked 503. Names no course, assignment or count: the role alone gives no access to a work (C-23).

Submission overview for each student visible to the caller, with a UTC minute and the record state from the signed receipt. A recorded submission awaiting its receipt has a null evidenceRecord. This read opens no work and returns no work text, hash or submission id. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns the same empty list as an assignment with no students.

post.summary: teacher.submissions.get for many assignments in one snapshot (R1): one entry per distinct id, lowercase, in the order of first appearance. POST so the ids never land in a URL; the body is exactly {assignmentIds}, 0 to 500 UUIDs in any case (duplicates count), at most 32 KiB; any other key or a malformed id is 422 invalid_input. An assignment the caller does not teach, or that does not exist, is the same entry with an empty list, never 403 or 404; proving that over the database belongs to the handler. More than 500 assignments take several reads, each its own snapshot. A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503.

200.description: an entry per assignment, possibly with no rows

get.summary: The course roster and the state of each student's work per assignment. Course teachers see the course; group teachers see their own groups. A missing name pair or group is null. A document id links to the work when one exists. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed course id returns the same empty list as a course with no students.

The teacher's courses and their assignments (institution.list_teacher_courses). Courses by academic year descending, then name (hr collation), then id; assignments by due time, then title, then id. Each course carries its rule on AI help, which a new assignment may only keep or narrow.

post.summary: The teacher of the assignment extends its deadline for one student of it (scope one) or for all (scope all). dueAt must be later than the deadline in force; the reason all is only for scope all. existingSubmissionsUnchanged is true when a submission in the scope was already recorded: the extension leaves it as it is. Success follows the database commit. An inaccessible assignment or student returns 404; invalid input or an earlier deadline 422.

get.summary: The deadline extensions of an assignment, oldest first, for its teacher. reasonId is null on a record another teacher wrote. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

post.summary: The teacher's fast path through the works of one assignment (B-11, #757): per student the state of the work, its text as blocks and the same process summary the student sees. POST so the assignment id never lands in a URL; the body is exactly {assignmentId}, a UUID in any case, at most 1 KiB; any other key or a malformed id is 422 invalid_input. An assignment the caller does not teach, or that does not exist, is the same empty list, never 403 or 404. Named students by surname, given name (hr) and id, then the unnamed by id.

The confirmed teacher to whom an open request was made approves or declines it. An optional decline reason has 1 to 600 Unicode code points and contains a non-whitespace character. It is kept in the audit record. Success follows the database commit; a closed request returns 409.

get.summary: The open mentorship requests made to the confirmed, unrevoked teacher in the caller's institution. A student without a name pair has a null name. The decision reason stays in the audit record.
One open mentorship of the caller as mentor. Another institution's, an ended one, an unknown and a malformed id all read the same 404.
The open mentorships of the caller as mentor, newest first; anyone else gets the same empty list. No time, activity or count of a work.

The ZIP of a ready Merlin package as application/zip, for the teacher who asked for it while teaching the assignment, before its expiry; the download is recorded in the same transaction that reads the bytes. The ZIP holds merlin-popis.csv (teacher.merlin-roster-csv.get), the PDF and DOCX of every submitted work under the names the CSV gives, and otisci.sha256 (one line per file: SHA-256, two spaces, name). Content-Disposition names the file merlin-paket.zip; X-Content-SHA256 is the SHA-256 of the ZIP, as teacher.merlin-package.get names it. A package not yet built or failed returns 409, an expired one 410; errors as teacher.merlin-package.get, as JSON.

200.description: ZIP bytes (application/zip); the contract format has no binary body

get.summary: The state of a Merlin package the caller asked for, while the caller teaches the assignment. A ready package names its download path, its expiry (24 hours after the build) and the SHA-256 of the ZIP; an expired one its expiry and SHA-256, without a path. A package of another teacher, of another assignment, unknown or malformed returns 404; a cross-site read 403.

post.summary: The teacher of the assignment asks for its Merlin package with a request key of the client's (8 to 128 of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, - and _). A new key makes a package and the server builds it; the same key again answers the same package and never builds a second one (a failed package is built again). The answer follows the build: ready, failed, or queued while another request is building it; expired once 24 hours have passed since the build. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment returns 404.

get.summary: The rows of teacher.merlin-roster.get as text/csv; charset=utf-8 (RFC 4180, CRLF, UTF-8 byte order mark): a header from the message catalogue (locales/merlin.ts) and the same columns in the same order. A null is an empty cell, true and false are the catalogue's yes and no words; a cell a spreadsheet would read as a formula starts with an apostrophe. No extension reasons. Content-Disposition names the file merlin-popis.csv. Errors as teacher.merlin-roster.get, as JSON.

200.description: CSV bytes (text/csv; charset=utf-8); the contract format has no text body

get.summary: The Merlin roster of an assignment for its teacher (D-286): one row per student by surname (Croatian alphabet), then given name; a student without a name pair last. Columns: surname, given name, submitted, the submission minute, after the deadline (with an approved extension, as the submission recorded it), and the names and SHA-256 fingerprints of the PDF and DOCX of the submitted revision in the package; null for a student without a submission. extensionReasons are the caller's own deadline extension records (N-13), oldest first. Nothing from the process summary and no private criterion. The read writes the teacher's opening of each work to the access log. A cross-site read is 403; an inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment 404; reads that disagree 503.

200.description: the roster, possibly with no rows

get.summary: Download the same PDF as the student, for a reader authorized to see this submission. No signed receipt, no relation to the work or a malformed id returns 404.

200.description: PDF bytes encoded in standard Base64, with a download filename

get.summary: The same submission state and signed receipt as student.submission.get, for a student the caller may read. The read has no work content and writes nothing to the access log (P-5). Inaccessible, unknown and malformed ids return the same 404.

Which students of an assignment submitted, with the work each row links to, for the assignment's teacher; one row per student with an open membership, by student id. Anyone else, an unknown or a malformed id gets the same empty list. No text, name, exact time, deadline, hash or submission id.

The six criteria of the caller's own working note on a work, always in the same order, with a null assessment and note where nothing is set. Only the teacher of the work who wrote them reads them; the student, another teacher, an unknown work and a malformed id all read the same 404. The read writes nothing in the access log.

put.summary: Sets the assessment and the note of one criterion, replacing both: a null clears it, and a criterion with neither reads as not set. Answers the saved criterion. Only the teacher of the work; the student, another teacher, an unknown work and an unknown criterion read the same 404.

get.summary: Read an attachment as standard Base64 after authorization against the work that owns the attachment and verification of the stored bytes. An unknown or inaccessible attachment returns 404.

200.description: Verified image bytes and attachment reference

post.summary: Upload a PNG or JPEG of up to 5 MiB with standard Base64. The server derives the type and SHA-256 from the bytes. Repeating the same bytes in the same work returns the existing attachment.

Adds a text to a consultation record of the work. Exactly {text}, at most 8 KiB. An empty or blank text is 422; a record that is not this work's reads as 404. Answers 201 with the addition and its whole-minute time.

get.summary: The consultation records of a work, oldest meeting first, each with its additions in the order they were made. The same list for the owner and the teacher of the assignment. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

post.summary: Records a consultation about a work: the day it was held, the revision it is about (a revision of the same work), a topic and the agreement. Exactly those four fields, at most 8 KiB. An empty topic, a date that does not exist or a revision of another work is 422. Answers 201 with the record, which has no additions yet.

get.summary: List the consultation slots of an accessible work, ordered by startsAt and id. proposedAt is the instant the student first requested the slot.

post.summary: The owning student requests a consultation at the given time.

patch.summary: The teacher confirms or replaces startsAt with a counter-proposal. The owning student accepts that time. proposedAt remains the instant of the original request.

get.summary: The short messages of a work, oldest first in the order of writing (the same order on every reading), at most 1000: the same conversation for the student of the work and the teachers of its assignment. senderRole is the role the author had when writing. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

post.summary: Writes a short message to the conversation of a work: {text}, 1 to 2000 characters with a non-space, NFC, no control character but newline and tab, no bidi control, at most 4 KiB, sent as application/json. It answers 201 with the stored message, as the list gives it. An empty or blank message is 422 and writes nothing; so is the 1001st message of a work. The student of the work and the teachers of its assignment write; another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

get.summary: The configured milestones of one work, in workflow order, for its owner and teachers.

200.description: Configured milestones with the current deadlines of this work

patch.summary: A teacher changes the deadline of one configured milestone of an unsubmitted work.

get.summary: One page of the versions of a work, newest first (revision descending, the submission before the checkpoint of its revision), at most 200: the saved points of the document up to the submitted revision and the submission. The same list for the owner and the teacher of the assignment; a teacher's read writes the access log. beforeRevision, from nextBeforeRevision of the previous page, asks for the versions below that revision; a revision is never split across two pages. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

200.description: one page of versions, possibly empty
